I am 76 years old. I farmed this land for 40 years. I only went to primary school, but I know my fields better than any young agronomist.

Here is what I do this year, same as most years — why change what works?

**Wheat (winter, about 10 mu):**
Last October I planted after the maize came off. I use improved wheat seed from the agro-shop in town — the shopkeeper Old Wang sells the same variety to everyone in our village, and everyone gets good harvest from it. About 15 kg seed per mu, drilled in by the machine I rent from my nephew.

For fertilizer, I put down 1 bag (50 kg) of compound 15-15-15 per mu as base when sowing. Then when wheat turns green in spring and starts jointing, I broadcast half a bag of urea, about 25 kg per mu. My neighbor Old Li puts on more, but I think this is enough. If I put too little, the wheat turns yellow and I lose money — better one extra handful than one short.

I water 4 times: once before winter (winter water is important, old people always say so), once at green-up, once at jointing, once at grain filling. My well still works fine, I paid for it 15 years ago.

Spray 2 times — once for aphids and rust together in spring, once before heading if I see powdery mildew.

I use the rotary tiller before sowing — plough is too much work at my age and the soil here doesn't need deep turning every year.

I expect about 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 460, the year before 430. It depends on the rain in May.

**Maize (summer, about 10 mu):**
After wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize right away — no-till, straight into the wheat stubble. Everyone here does it this way now, saves water and time. The hybrid seed is Zhengdan or similar, whatever Old Wang recommends that year. About 2 kg seed per mu.

At planting I put one bag compound (40 kg) per mu as base. Then when maize is knee-high, I side-dress 25 kg urea per mu. Maize is hungry, especially when it's tasseling.

I water 2 times if rain is poor — once at big-trumpet stage, once at grain filling. If rain comes, I skip.

Spray 2 times — one for corn borer, one for armyworm if I see it.

I expect 550 kg per mu. My land is flat and the well is close, so maize does well here.
